# Architecture overview

Zinux uses a **hybrid microkernel** model (inspired by seL4, Graphene, and Fuchsia): a small trusted core plus isolated components that communicate through capability-checked IPC.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        User space                            │
│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐    │
│  │  shell   │  │   init   │  │  drivers │  │ plugins  │    │
│  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘  └────┬─────┘    │
│       └─────────────┴─────────────┴─────────────┘           │
│                         │ IPC (capability syscalls)        │
├─────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Kernel interface (syscall)                │
├─────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │              Microkernel core                        │    │
│  │  • processes & threads    • memory (PMM/VMM)         │    │
│  │  • scheduler              • IPC & capabilities       │    │
│  │  • interrupts             • timer                    │    │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
│  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐       │
│  │ arch/x86_64  │  │   drivers/   │  │   lib/       │       │
│  │ (GDT, IDT,   │  │ (VGA, UART,  │  │ (ring buffer,│       │
│  │  paging,     │  │  keyboard,   │  │  bitmap,     │       │
│  │  context sw) │  │  timer, PCI) │  │  log, fmt)   │       │
│  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Design principles

| Principle | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|
| **Almost 100% Zig** | No separate `.S` files for logic; inline `asm volatile` only where Zig cannot reach (e.g. `lgdt`, `iretq`). |
| **Over-documentation** | Every line explains its reasoning — see `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`. The kernel reads like a textbook. |
| **Clarity over performance** | Working, understandable code first; optimize only after measurement. |
| **Freestanding-first** | No `std` in the kernel; its own module tree. |
| **Testability** | QEMU integration tests in CI; host unit tests where possible. |
| **Multi-arch readiness** | x86_64 first; interfaces abstracted under `arch/`. |

## Technology choices

| Component | Choice | Why |
|-----------|--------|-----|
| Language | Zig 0.16+ | comptime, explicit integers, cross-compile, simple build |
| Bootloader | Limine | UEFI/BIOS, SMP, framebuffer, higher-half ready |
| Target | `x86_64-freestanding-none` | Widest ecosystem, QEMU support |
| Linker | LLD via Zig, `linker.ld` | Higher-half kernel |
| Emulator | QEMU 9.x | CI integration tests |
| ISO | xorriso + Limine | Bootable image |
| Reproducibility | `.zigversion` + `build.zig.zon` | Pinned toolchain |

## Repository map

```
zinux/
├── build.zig / build.zig.zon / .zigversion
├── linker.ld / limine.conf
├── kernel/     # main.zig, boot/, arch/x86_64/, mm/, sched/, ipc/,
│               # drivers/, syscall/, plugin/, snapshot*.zig, fs/, net/
├── userland/   # init, shell, lib/, *_test ELFs, vsl/, composer/
├── libs/       # zinuxabi.zig — shared kernel/user ABI
├── tests/      # host/ unit tests, fixtures
├── tools/      # ISO builder, plugin verifier, generators
└── docs/       # architecture, roadmap, specs (this book's sources)
```

The following chapters walk this map one layer at a time, always in the same order: concept, mechanism, files, lab.
